subject: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — Aurora Retail
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@aurora-retail.com>

Subject: Discovery follow-up & stakeholder mapping

Thanks for the demo today, Marissa — that was really helpful. Quick follow-ups from our side as we start internal alignment:

- Use case: customer support ticket classification + routing (pilot scope: US contact center).
- Immediate asks from procurement/security/legal:
  1) Who is the economic owner for approvals (finance / line-of-business)?
  2) Security needs a short evidence pack (SOC 2, data encryption, data flow diagram).
  3) Procurement needs the expected contract flow and typical SLAs / termination terms.
  4) We need an org chart to identify the legal/procurement contacts and the executive sponsor.

I've attached a high-level org chart (aurora_org_chart_v2.pdf). Looping in Devon (IT Security) and Priya (Procurement) here for their inputs — they're copied on this thread.

Can you map Redwood contacts to these roles and share a suggested intro chain? Also appreciate a short checklist of the security artifacts we should prepare.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Head of Technical Programs
Aurora Retail

From: Devon Carter <devon@aurora-retail.com>

Thanks — quick security notes from my side:

- Primary concerns: data residency for logs, PII handling, encryption in transit & at rest, access controls, and incident response expectations.
- For initial review we need: SOC 2 Type II report (or SOC 2 roadmap if in progress), data flow diagram showing where tokens/logs are stored/processed, description of how Redwood isolates customer data across tenants, and details on KMS/HSM usage.
- Also please include retention policies for request/response logs and the redact/PII-handling approach.

If you can send a short zip of the artifacts or a secure link, I'll route to our security review board. If a SOC 2 isn't available yet, a security brief + controls table is fine for initial gating.

Devon Carter
Director, IT Security
Aurora Retail

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Devon Carter <devon@aurora-retail.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha@aurora-retail.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, alex_martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up & stakeholder mapping

Devon / Samantha — appreciate the clarity, Devon. Attached is a short security brief that covers the main controls and where to find supporting evidence (redwood-security-brief.pdf). Quick highlights below for your immediate review:

- SOC 2: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II; we can provide the report under an NDA.
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest; customer-managed KMS supported for Private deployments.
- Data flow: request routing happens in-region for hosted customers; KV cache and logs are stored with customer isolation. We redact PII by default in logs where requested and provide configurable retention windows.
- Access & auditing: role-based access, full audit logs, and optional integration with your SIEM.

Next steps we propose:
1) We’ll provide the SOC 2 pack and a concise data flow diagram in a secure share (link to follow).
2) Rishi will be your point for technical security calls — he can join the sync next week.
3) Samantha — once you share procurement/legal names we’ll prepare sample contract language and an order-of-magnitude SOW for the pilot.

Available meeting windows (PT): Tue 11/16 1–3pm, Wed 11/17 2–4pm. Which of those works?

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to the security review and pilot scoping phase.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-security-brief.pdf
